description:
How many elements `list_elements` serves you, by type: the number you
reach by paging it to its end with the same arguments. Ask the size of a
world here.

With no `type`: every one of the 22 types, 0 included. With `type` (a slug
from `list_element_types`): that type only. `name_contains`, `supertype`,
`subtype`, `ids`, `created_by`, `link`, `include_room` and
`include_proposed` are list_elements' own and filter as there; `link`
needs a `type`. Requires a READ or WRITE API-Key. Returns `{counts: {type:
n, ...}, total, proposed_left_out, room_left_out}`; `total` is the sum of
`counts`.
A parlor's room elements (marked `x_room_of`) are left out unless
`include_room` is true, and so are the world's reading aids (its Charter,
Guide and Domains, marked `x_charter_of`). `room_left_out` is how many room
elements and reading aids turning `include_room` on adds (0 with
`include_room`); in a world with no parlor, all it counts is reading aids.
An element carrying x_review_proposed is proposed, not yet reviewed by a
keeper; it is left out unless asked for. `proposed_left_out` is how many
proposed elements turning `include_proposed` on adds (0 with
`include_proposed`).
Each left-out number is what its own flag adds, with the other flag as you
set it. A proposed element that is also a room element or a reading aid is
in neither number: it comes back only with both flags true. So for every
proposed element, read `proposed_left_out` with `include_room` true; for
everything you may read, read `total` with both flags true. An edit held for
review as a proposal is not an element: it is in no number here.
A key or a sign-in counts only what it may read; a stub (`known_of`)
counts as one element.

world.description: The world to read, by id or by its public page's slug. With an API-Key, leave it out (or name the key's own world by its id): a key reads its own world only. list_worlds names the worlds you can read here.

name: count_elements
